clue.text: Share rooms as house turned somewhat cold at first

indicators.note: this places the cold piece at the very front, ahead of everything else in the chain

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: something turned faces the other way, so the abbreviation is read from right to left

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
somewhat means a bit, slightly

explanation.surface: Flatmates share rooms while the house they live in is chilly at first.
explanation.definitionFit: To live together under one roof, especially as a couple, is to share living quarters with somebody.

clue.text: Policeman is on to drug deal

parts.note: a cop is a policeman
E is short for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: A police officer has found out about a drugs transaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' looks like a noun, a drug deal, but it is the verb, as in to deal with something.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage or handle a difficulty is to deal with it, and to cope with it.

clue.text: Find refuge in boat — that's the most advisable policy

indicators.note: in places the refuge word inside the vessel word

parts.note: a hoy is a small coastal sailing boat or barge
to nest is to settle in a safe home

explanation.surface: Sheltering in a boat is the wisest course of action.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to the proverb 'honesty is the best policy'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says that being truthful is the best policy, so it is the most advisable one.

clue.text: We hear insect chewed leaf

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, so its sound matters, not its spelling

parts.note: an insect with hard wing cases; said aloud it matches the leaf

explanation.surface: Apparently a bug has nibbled a leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewed' looks like what the insect did, but it belongs to the definition: the leaf people chew.
explanation.definitionFit: Betel is the leaf of an Asian vine, wrapped round areca nut and chewed as a mild stimulant.

clue.text: Mock Turtle's first at party, a scene of debauchery

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: opening letter of Turtle
a rave is a large dance party
a sty, a pigsty, is a place of filth and depravity

explanation.surface: The Mock Turtle from Alice in Wonderland turns up at a wild party.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mock Turtle is a character in Alice in Wonderland, but 'Mock' is detached as the definition, a noun meaning a parody.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque imitation, a mockery of the real thing.

clue.text: Being divorced? On your head be it

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a separation, the act of going separate ways
second meaning, read literally: the line combed through the hair sits on your head

explanation.walkthrough: 'On your head be it' is an idiom for taking the blame; here it is read literally, as something that is on top of your head.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a separation of partners, and also the line where hair is combed in two directions.

clue.text: Summary showing one switch in prices

indicators.note: a switch is a swap of places, so one letter changes position in the word

parts.note: the word whose letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A short report shows that one change has been made to prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is the letter I: it swaps places with the E, and nothing else moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A précis is a short summary giving the main points of a longer text.

clue.text: Put down, say, in similar surroundings

indicators.note: in places the example abbreviation inside the word for similar
the word for similar acts as surroundings, wrapping around the short abbreviation

parts.note: things that are similar are related
say means for example, abbreviated e.g.

explanation.surface: Something is set down, for instance, among others like it.
explanation.walkthrough: Relegation is a soccer term: a team that finishes low is sent down to a lower division.
explanation.definitionFit: To be relegated is to be moved down to a lower rank or division, so put down.

clue.text: Accustomed to admit head of security under cover

indicators.note: to admit someone is to let them in, so the word for accustomed takes a letter inside

parts.note: inured means hardened or accustomed to something

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: opening letter of security

explanation.surface: Someone used to letting in a chief of security works undercover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under cover' looks like spying, but it means covered by an insurance policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being protected by an insurance policy is being under cover, as insurers call it cover.

clue.text: Some may be forced inside it-the effect is disastrous

definitions.text: Some may be forced inside it-the effect is disastrous

parts.words: Some may be forced inside it
parts.note: surface reading: people pushed into a place against their will
setter's reading: plants grown early under glass, and the warming of the planet named after that glass building

explanation.walkthrough: Gardeners force plants, bringing them on early under glass; and the climate effect named after the glass building is disastrous.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass building for growing plants, which also names the effect that traps heat in Earth's atmosphere.

clue.text: Mark my words

parts.note: surface reading: a warning to remember what I say
setter's reading: put commas and full stops into my text

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a stock warning ('take note of what I say'), but read literally it asks someone to put marks into written words.
explanation.definitionFit: To insert commas, full stops and other marks into writing is exactly to mark a text's words.

clue.text: Getting some boll-weevil is lethal for cotton

indicators.note: taking only some of the following words means the letters lie inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of weevil, all of is and the start of lethal

explanation.surface: A cotton farmer learns that the boll-weevil, a beetle that eats cotton buds, is deadly to the crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, strong cotton thread, once used for stockings, named after the French city Lille.

clue.text: One's left army job — press one to join up when the heat is on

definitions.text: one to join up when the heat is on

indicators.note: having left means the single numeral one has walked out of the word that follows

parts.note: working as a soldier is an army job
one is the Roman numeral I, which is removed
to press clothes is to iron them

explanation.surface: Someone quits the army and is pushed to enlist again just when things get tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'join up' and 'heat is on' sound like army recruitment under pressure; they really describe a hot tool joining metal.
explanation.definitionFit: This hot tool melts metal alloy to join wires and components together, so it unites things when heated.

clue.text: Cancelling a bit of golf? That's unpleasant

parts.note: a cancelled event is off
putting, tapping the ball towards the hole, is one part of golf

explanation.surface: A golfer grumbles at having part of their round cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something off-putting is disagreeable or disconcerting, making you less keen.

clue.text: Use Franklin's experimental method to test opinion

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Benjamin Franklin sent one up in a storm to study lightning
second meaning: float an idea to see how people react

explanation.surface: A scientist borrows Franklin's approach to find out what people think.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both Franklin's famous lightning experiment with a string and key, and an idiom for trying out an idea on others.

clue.text: What one discovers — it's not safe to be small

definitions.text: What one discovers — it's not safe to be small

parts.note: the plain sense: whatever a person finds out

parts.words: it's not safe to be small
parts.note: allusion to the proverb that a little learning is a dangerous thing

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb runs 'a little ___ is a dangerous thing', so the small amount of it is the unsafe one.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning and awareness are what you gain by finding things out, and the proverb warns that a little is dangerous.

clue.text: I dust, moving round in room

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift position, so the opening words are rearranged

parts.note: these five letters rearranged
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone doing the housework moves about a room with a duster.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is a workroom for an artist or photographer, or a one-room flat.

clue.text: Isn't it ever left rumpled in bed?

definitions.text: Isn't it ever left rumpled in bed?

parts.words: Isn't it ever left rumpled in bed?
parts.note: surface reading: a complaint about an untidy sleeper

parts.words: Isn't it ever left rumpled in bed?
parts.note: setter's reading: the bedspread that lies on top of the bed and gets crumpled

explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems to nag about a messy person, but 'it' is the bedspread on top, which is often left creased.
explanation.definitionFit: A coverlet is a bedspread, the top layer laid over a made bed.

clue.text: Caring type has gone to other extremes

parts.note: gone by is past

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of other

explanation.surface: A kind-hearted person has gone off in the opposite direction to extremes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor is a minister who looks after a congregation; pastoral care is the caring side of the job.

clue.text: Son's taken over helm, it being less stormy

indicators.note: the son has taken over, sitting at the front ahead of the steering word

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a tiller is the lever that steers a boat

explanation.surface: A son takes the helm of a boat once the weather has calmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that is calmer and more tranquil than before is still-er, comparatively still.

clue.text: Has round trip to American state

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so the letters fall about into a new order

parts.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A traveller makes a round trip to somewhere in the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American state' suggests one of the fifty US states; here it is a nation in Central America.
explanation.definitionFit: Honduras is an independent country in Central America, so it is a state on the American continent.

clue.text: Unusual piece of information revealing regional dish

parts.note: rare means uncommon
a bit is a unit of information in computing

explanation.surface: An odd fact comes to light about a local delicacy.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is melted cheese on toast, a dish linked to Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast, a food associated with one region of Britain.

clue.text: Constant is given for child's second name, actually

indicators.note: one thing given for another takes its place, so a letter is swapped out

parts.note: an infant is a young child
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
the second N, the letter abbreviating name, is the one replaced

explanation.surface: A child's middle name is replaced by one that is constant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second name' looks like a middle name; it means the second N in the word for child, N being short for name.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means really or as a matter of truth, the same as actually.

clue.text: Hit-and-miss procedure producing miscarriage of justice?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: learning by trying things until one works
second meaning, read literally: a court hearing followed by a mistake

explanation.surface: A haphazard legal process ends up wrongly convicting someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second reading: a court case plus a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a method of finding solutions by repeated attempts, and literally a court hearing plus a mistake.

clue.text: Part of rider's equipment, lower if you switch sides

indicators.note: switching sides swaps left for right, so those two letters trade places

parts.note: the word taken as written; its L and R are swapped

explanation.surface: A piece of a horseman's kit could be lowered if moved across.
explanation.walkthrough: Sides are L and R, left and right: change one for the other at each end.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowel is the spiked revolving wheel on the end of a rider's spur.

clue.text: Some girls quail when in a group

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gathering of young women
second meaning: the collective noun for these birds

explanation.surface: Some girls lose their nerve when they are together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quail' looks like the verb, to flinch, but it is the game bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a collective noun for a flock of quail and for a lively gathering of girls or women.

clue.text: At one time I was first, but stopped making an effort

parts.note: I'd, short for I had, looking back to an earlier time
to be first in a race is to have led

explanation.surface: A runner who was once in front has eased off.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to do nothing much or coast, so someone who has idled has stopped working hard.

clue.text: Nothing needing to be paid yet? That's OK

definitions.text: Nothing needing to be paid yet
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read in two words: every debt is still merely owing

explanation.surface: A relieved debtor hears that no bill is due yet, and says that suits them.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as ALL OWABLE: if everything can still be owed, nothing has to be paid now.
explanation.definitionFit: Something permitted by the rules is acceptable, which is what OK means.

clue.text: Chap covering sleeve of coat, for example

indicators.note: something covering another goes around it, so the man's word wraps the limb word

parts.note: a chap is a gent, a gentleman
a sleeve is the arm of a coat

explanation.surface: A man has his coat sleeve over his arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat is one example of an item of clothing, an article worn on the body.

clue.text: Author labours after one's rejected play

indicators.note: after places the word for labours in front of the word for play
the numeral one is rejected, thrown out of the word for labours

parts.note: to labour is to toil
one is the Roman numeral I, which is removed
to play with something is to toy with it

explanation.surface: A writer works hard after their play is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' reads as if labours follows play, but it means labours (less one) comes after nothing: it simply leads, with play tacked on behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo Tolstoy was the Russian novelist who wrote War and Peace and Anna Karenina.
